item.title: Navigating Disability: Perspectives and Practices in Indonesian Religious Courts
item.description: This study explores how disability is defined and addressed in Indonesia’s Islamic religious courts, drawing on court decisions from the Direktori Putusan Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia (Directory of Supreme Court Decisions of the Republic of Indonesia) spanning 2005 to 2023. item.title: From the Balkans to Istanbul: The Legal Politics of Social Mobilities through Devshirme in the Ottoman Empire from the 14th to the 17th Century
item.description: The Ottoman Empire rose to prominence as a dominant force from the 13th to the 19th centuries, establishing a vast empire and nurturing cultures that continue to enrich global heritage today. A notable feature of their sociopolitical structure was the practice of devshirme. item.title: Reframing Islamic Family Law Through Web-Based Tafsir: The Case of Nushuz in the Indonesian Tafsir Online
item.description: One of the most effective strategies for disseminating tafsīr al-aḥkām today is through digital platforms, particularly Islamic web portals. These sites offer accessible, thematic, and concise interpretations that appeal to diverse audiences, especially on gender-sensitive issues such as nushūz, which has often been read in ways that marginalize women’s rights. item.description: Cairo’s astronomical manuscripts (falak) are abundant, yet many remain understudied and insufficiently analyzed in contemporary scholarship. item.title: Female Leadership of Islamic Philanthropic Institutions in Indonesia
item.description: This study aims to examine the experiences of female leaders in Islamic philanthropy in managing zakat in Indonesia from the perspective of Maqāṣid al-Sharīʿah and gender justice. item.title: The History of the Malay Fiqh Development: An Analysis of the Manuscript ‘Qawānīn al-Mubtadi’fī al-Fiqh’ Work by Abdurrahman Husin al-Kelantani, Mufti of ‘Amantubillah’
item.description: This study examines the development of Malay fiqh by analyzing the manuscript Qawānīn al-Mubtadi’ fī al-Fiqh by the Mufti of Mempawah, Abdurrahman Husin al-Kelantani. item.title: Deconstructing Misogynistic Interpretations: A Gender-Just Fiqh Approach to the Role of Women in Family and Career
item.description: This study focuses on gender injustice within families, particularly as experienced by women working in environments where misogynistic ideologies continue to dominate and shape domestic relations. item.title: The Oran Fatwa as an Emergency Fiqh Strategy Addressing the 16th-Century Identity Crisis of Morisco Muslims
item.description: The Oran fatwa, issued by Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah al-Maghrāwī in the early 16th century, emerged as a religious response to the tragic circumstances faced by the Morisco Muslims in Spain following the fall of Granada. This fatwa provides legal guidance for Muslims who maintained their faith while being outwardly compelled to adhere to Catholic practices.
